children: By Kit Norton and Anita Hamilton

DoorDash on Thursday agreed to acquire Instacart for $17 billion as the company makes a big move to hold off Amazon.com and Walmart. The possibility of such a deal was previously reported last week, but the companies only disclosed the specifics today.

The acquisition could help the combined companies stave off growing competition in the online grocery delivery space. While Instacart is currently the leader, it was unclear how long it could retain its top spot.

"The durability of Instacart's leadership position in grocery delivery is softening, even as the broader online category remains healthy," Rosenblatt's Scott Devitt noted before the deal was announced.

Shares of DoorDash rose more than 6% to $180, with Instacart falling by less than 1% to $58. Shares of Uber Technologies, whose Uber Eats service competes with both firms and which had reportedly been considering a purchase as well, were flat.

The stock price bump for DoorDash also coincided with its solid earnings beat in the third quarter. It earnings came in at $1.06 a share, well ahead of the 81 cents analysts had estimated. Revenue was $4.62 billion, ahead of the $4.56 billion expected among those polled by FactSet.
DoorDash said it would acquire Instacart for $65 a share, which represents a 11% premium from Instacart stock's closing price of $58.42 on Wednesday.
The deal represents a premium of 26% from Instacart's closing price of $51.68 a share on Oct. 22, which was the last trading day before media reports emerged about a possible transaction.
DoorDash said the deal will be at least 75% in cash and expects to fund that portion with cash on hand and proceeds from debt financing.
Wall Street's initial response was to cheer on the acquisition but time will tell if DoorDash can hold off those two titans.
